metadata.name: data_ai_behavior_gold_32
metadata.purpose: Small high-quality behavioral Gold Test candidate covering ambiguity, context, normalization, known and unseen variants, and no-change decisions.
metadata.relationship_to_retrieval_gold: Separate from data_ai_retrieval_gold_50.json. This file tests normalization/decision behavior, not Recall@K retrieval alone.
metadata.design_principle: Quality, diversity, correctness, and clear gold decisions are prioritized over dataset size.

case_types.ambiguous: Surface form can express more than one concept; context must determine the intended sense.
case_types.known_variant: A variant/alias/abbreviation already recorded in the terminology resource.
case_types.unseen_variant: A source-attested form observed in real pilot evidence but not registered in aliases/abbreviations/variants.
case_types.context_required: The surrounding sentence is necessary to make the intended sense clear.
case_types.canonical_or_no_change: The canonical term is already correct in context and should be preserved.
case_types.do_not_normalize: The surface form resembles a terminology entry but is being used in another sense and must not be normalized.

expected_actions.NORMALIZE_TO_CANONICAL: Replace/resolve the trigger to the expected canonical terminology entry.
expected_actions.KEEP_CANONICAL: The canonical terminology entry is correctly used; keep it unchanged.
expected_actions.DO_NOT_NORMALIZE: Do not map this occurrence to the technical terminology entry.

data_policy: No case is copied verbatim from positive_examples, negative_examples, or generated_examples.
Test sentences are human-authored from Siwar definitions and documented real usage/competing senses in the pilot.
Unseen variants are source-attested in real pilot evidence but absent from registered variant fields.
This file is evaluation-only and must not be added to the retrieval corpus or training/enrichment data.
Researcher review is required before reporting this as a final expert-validated Gold Test.
